dimensions.assessment: Affects newly public companies, emerging growth companies, and financial market regulators.
dimensions.evidence: small, newly public companies (i.e., emerging growth companies)

dimensions.assessment: Reduces financial disclosure and regulatory compliance burdens for companies with revenues up to $3 billion for a longer duration.
dimensions.evidence: allows emerging growth companies to continue operating under these regulations for an additional five years

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state or imply direct federal spending or revenue changes.
Amends the Securities Act of 1933 and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 by updating statutory definitions and thresholds.
dimensions.evidence: Section 2(a)(19) of the Securities Act of 1933... Section 3(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory amendment altering reporting criteria and timelines for qualifying corporate issuers.

missing_information: Exact count of additional corporations that would qualify as emerging growth companies under the $3 billion threshold
importance_detail.rationale: The bill expands securities regulation exemptions for emerging growth companies by raising their annual gross revenue limit to $3 billion, extending transition periods to 10 years, and removing the large accelerated filer restriction.
